objectives.description: Explain the nature of solar energy, how the sun produces energy, and Nigeria's solar energy potential
Describe renewable energy sources and compare solar energy with other energy sources (fossil fuels, wind, hydro)
Identify electrical safety rules and apply them when working with solar equipment and live circuits
Describe basic electrical concepts including voltage, current, resistance, and power relevant to solar systems
Identify the main components of a solar PV system: solar panels, charge controller, battery, and inverter
Explain how a photovoltaic solar panel converts sunlight to electricity and describe types of PV panels
Describe the function of a charge controller and explain how it protects batteries from overcharging
Describe types of batteries used in solar systems, their maintenance needs, and safety precautions
Explain the function of an inverter and distinguish between AC and DC electricity in solar systems
Conduct a basic site assessment to determine the suitability of a location for solar panel installation
Mount solar panels correctly on a rooftop or ground frame at the appropriate tilt angle for Nigeria
Wire solar panels in series and parallel configurations and connect components of a basic solar system
Perform simple solar system installation for a small off-grid application (lighting, phone charging)
Perform routine maintenance on solar PV systems including panel cleaning, connection checks, and battery testing
Diagnose and troubleshoot common solar system faults including no output, low voltage, and battery drain
Describe the business opportunities in solar energy installation and maintenance in Nigeria
Calculate basic energy load requirements for a household and size a simple solar system to meet them
